name: Derma roller (home)

lead: A home derma roller is a handheld roller covered in tiny needles, usually 0.25 to 0.5 millimeters at home, rolled across the skin to create microscopic punctures. It is a consumer version of professional microneedling.
It is promoted for scars, texture, fine lines and better absorption of serums.

paras: Needle punctures trigger a wound-healing response that increases collagen and elastin production in the dermis. Professional devices use longer needles to reach deeper layers, while shorter home needles are reported to produce less effect.

Home use carries a risk of infection, irritation, post-inflammatory pigmentation and scarring if the roller is not sterilized or technique is poor. Reviews note that proper sterilization is essential for home rollers. The collagen evidence is for professional microneedling, not home rolling, and no systematic review of home rollers specifically was found.
